title: Advanced DFV Practice and Leadership
description: This module supports experienced practitioners and leaders to strengthen advanced DFV capabilities. It focuses on complex case practice, supervision, system leadership, and driving high-quality, evidence-informed responses.
outcomes: Apply advanced DFV practice in complex situations
Provide effective supervision and practice leadership
Lead system improvements and evidence-informed practice

title: Advanced Risk Management
description: This module equips specialist DFV practitioners with advanced skills in assessing, monitoring, and responding to high-risk and rapidly changing domestic and family violence situations. It focuses on lethality assessment, multi-agency risk panels, and dynamic risk monitoring.
outcomes: Conduct advanced lethality assessments using specialist frameworks
Participate effectively in multi-agency risk panels and high-risk teams
Monitor and respond to dynamic and rapidly changing DFV risk

title: Assessment and Response
description: This module builds practitioner capability in conducting safe, structured, and trauma‑informed DFV assessments. It covers initial screening, risk identification, and collaborative safety planning with clients.
outcomes: Conduct safe and effective DFV screening and assessment
Identify key DFV risk indicators and patterns
Develop collaborative and practical safety plans with clients

title: Boundaries and Safety
description: This module supports peer mentors to maintain strong personal and professional boundaries while providing safe, ethical, and sustainable peer support. It covers boundary-setting, self-care, and the use of supervision to prevent burnout and vicarious trauma.
outcomes: Maintain clear and consistent boundaries in peer support relationships
Use self-care strategies to manage emotional load and prevent burnout
Engage in supervision and support structures to ensure safe practice

title: Building Respectful Communities
description: This module supports communities to build cultures of respect, equality, and safety. It focuses on positive social norms, community leadership, and everyday actions that prevent violence.
outcomes: Promote respect and equality in community settings
Identify positive norms that prevent violence
Engage community members in everyday prevention actions

title: Bystander Action and Community Safety
description: This module equips community members with the skills to take safe, ethical, and effective bystander action when they witness or suspect DFV. It focuses on recognising warning signs, choosing safe intervention options, and promoting community responsibility.
outcomes: Recognise signs that someone may be experiencing or using DFV
Choose safe and appropriate bystander actions
Promote community responsibility for preventing DFV

title: Case Review and Reflective Practice
description: This module supports specialist DFV practitioners to engage in structured case review, reflective practice, and continuous improvement. It focuses on analysing complex cases, identifying learning themes, and strengthening professional judgement through reflective frameworks.
outcomes: Use structured case review processes to analyse complex DFV cases
Apply reflective practice frameworks to strengthen professional judgement
Identify learning themes and integrate them into ongoing practice improvement

title: Challenging Gender Inequality and Harmful Norms
description: This module explores how gender inequality and harmful social norms drive domestic and family violence. It supports learners to identify, challenge, and shift attitudes, beliefs, and structures that enable violence.
outcomes: Understand how gender inequality drives DFV
Recognise harmful norms and stereotypes
Apply strategies to challenge and shift harmful norms

title: Child-Centred and Family-Focused Practice
description: This module supports practitioners to place children at the centre of DFV responses while working with the whole family system. It focuses on balancing safety, accountability, and relational healing.
outcomes: Apply child-centred principles in DFV practice
Work with families while maintaining safety and accountability
Support relational healing and stability

title: Supporting Child Healing
description: This module helps parents understand how domestic and family violence affects children emotionally, behaviourally, and developmentally. It provides practical, age‑appropriate strategies to support children’s healing, resilience, and sense of safety.
outcomes: Understand how DFV impacts children at different developmental stages
Provide age‑appropriate emotional support to children recovering from DFV
Strengthen children’s resilience and sense of safety

title: Trauma‑Informed Client Engagement
description: This module strengthens practitioner capability in engaging clients using trauma‑informed, strengths‑based, and culturally safe approaches. It focuses on building trust, working with resistance, and supporting clients who may be overwhelmed, fearful, or ambivalent.
outcomes: Engage clients using trauma‑informed principles
Recognise and respond safely to resistance and ambivalence
Use strengths‑based approaches to support client empowerment

title: Collaboration and Referral Pathways

outcomes: Collaborate effectively with partner agencies and service systems
Use clear and accurate documentation to support client safety
Navigate referral pathways to connect clients with appropriate supports

outcomes: Understand the role of community accountability in preventing DFV
Promote community norms that challenge violence and support safety
Coordinate collective action to strengthen community responses

outcomes: Participate in or lead community DFV awareness activities
Build partnerships that strengthen local DFV prevention efforts
Amplify survivor voices safely, ethically, and without harm

description: This module equips community members and local groups to respond safely and effectively during DFV-related crises. It focuses on recognising immediate danger, supporting safety planning, and knowing when and how to escalate concerns.
outcomes: Recognise signs of immediate danger or escalating DFV risk
Support basic safety planning in community contexts
Know when and how to escalate concerns to services or authorities

title: Community Education and Prevention Campaigns
description: This module supports communities to design, deliver, and evaluate DFV prevention and awareness campaigns. It focuses on messaging, engagement strategies, and ensuring campaigns are safe, ethical, and culturally appropriate.
outcomes: Design community education activities that promote DFV awareness
Develop safe and ethical prevention messaging
Engage diverse community groups in prevention efforts

description: This module supports communities to understand and participate in collective healing after domestic and family violence. It focuses on trauma-aware community practices, rebuilding trust, and creating environments that support long-term recovery and resilience.
outcomes: Understand how communities experience and recover from collective trauma
Participate in trauma-aware community healing practices
Support environments that promote long-term recovery, resilience, and reconnection

title: Community Leadership for Change
description: This module supports community leaders, volunteers, and local influencers to drive positive change in preventing domestic and family violence. It focuses on leadership behaviours, mobilising communities, and sustaining long-term prevention efforts.
outcomes: Understand the role of community leadership in DFV prevention
Mobilise community members to participate in safety and prevention initiatives
Sustain long-term community-led change efforts

title: Community-Led Prevention Strategies
description: This module supports communities to design and lead their own DFV prevention strategies. It focuses on grassroots leadership, community strengths, and localised approaches that reflect cultural, social, and environmental contexts.
outcomes: Understand the value of community-led DFV prevention
Identify strengths and resources within local communities
Develop and implement community-driven prevention strategies

description: This module supports communities to build partnerships and coordinate local action to prevent domestic and family violence. It focuses on collaboration between community groups, services, and local leaders to create safer, more connected environments.
outcomes: Build effective partnerships between community groups, services, and local leaders
Coordinate local DFV prevention and safety initiatives
Strengthen community capacity to respond collectively to DFV

description: This module prepares practitioners to work with high‑risk, multi‑layered, and complex DFV cases. It covers advanced risk factors, trauma complexity, and navigating challenging family dynamics while maintaining safety, clarity, and professional boundaries.
outcomes: Identify and respond to high‑risk and complex DFV presentations
Work effectively with clients experiencing multi‑layered trauma
Navigate complex family dynamics while maintaining safety and clarity

description: This module equips specialist DFV practitioners with the knowledge and skills needed to support clients through court processes, protection order applications, and legal pathways. Prepare clients for court in a trauma-informed and safety-focused way
Work effectively with legal services, police, and court stakeholders

title: Cultural Safety in Community Responses
description: This module supports community members, volunteers, and local leaders to respond to DFV in culturally safe, respectful, and community-led ways. It focuses on understanding cultural contexts, avoiding assumptions, and building trust with diverse communities.
outcomes: Understand the importance of cultural safety in DFV responses
Recognise how cultural context shapes experiences of DFV and help-seeking
Engage respectfully and safely with diverse communities

title: Designing and Evaluating Prevention Initiatives
description: This module supports learners to design, implement, and evaluate primary prevention initiatives. It focuses on evidence-informed planning, monitoring, and continuous improvement.
outcomes: Design evidence-informed prevention initiatives
Monitor and evaluate prevention activities
Use data and feedback to improve prevention outcomes

description: This module provides an overview of the physical, psychological, reproductive, and long-term health impacts of domestic and family violence. It supports health and community workers to recognise DFV-related health presentations.

Identify DFV-related health presentations
Understand long-term health consequences of trauma and violence

Identify pathways to safety and stability for victim-survivors

Respond safely to disclosures in clinical settings
Use safe documentation and referral pathways

Identify and respond to tech-facilitated abuse in safe and appropriate ways

Challenge harmful norms and promote equality
Support youth-led initiatives and leadership

Respond safely and ethically to disclosures within faith communities
Promote faith environments that support safety, dignity, and equality

Recognise the values and principles that underpin safe and ethical work
Identify the knowledge and skills needed across different workforce roles

Increase parental confidence in responding to unsafe situations

description: This module supports parents who are navigating the challenges of parenting while experiencing domestic and family violence. It focuses on managing parental stress, supporting children’s emotional needs, and maintaining connection during instability.

description: This module supports practitioners to maintain ethical, safe, and sustainable DFV practice. It focuses on boundaries, confidentiality, reflective practice, and strategies to prevent burnout and vicarious trauma.

Avoid retraumatisation and maintain emotional safety during conversations

title: Strategic Partnerships and Sector Leadership
description: This module supports DFV leaders to build strategic partnerships, influence sector-wide practice, and contribute to systemic improvement. It focuses on collaboration, cross-sector leadership, and shaping policy and practice environments that strengthen safety and wellbeing.

outcomes: Support children’s emotional and physical safety

Strengthen protective relationships with safe caregivers

description: This module helps community members provide safe, respectful, and appropriate support to people experiencing DFV. It focuses on listening without judgement, validating experiences, and connecting people to appropriate services.
outcomes: Provide safe and supportive responses to community members experiencing DFV

Connect people to appropriate services without creating additional risk

outcomes: Maintain professional boundaries while responding to DFV

Use reflective practice to support safe and sustainable work

outcomes: Provide strengths-based emotional support to survivors
Help survivors understand and navigate available services
Encourage safe and appropriate help-seeking without giving advice outside the peer role

Advocate effectively for clients in complex or unsafe system interactions
Coordinate multi‑service responses to support client safety and wellbeing

Contribute to system reform through collaboration and feedback

Support healing and secure attachment

Identify protective factors that support recovery

Support clients through reporting, evidence, and risk processes

title: Working with LGBTQIA+ Communities
description: This module supports practitioners to understand and respond to DFV within LGBTQIA+ communities. It focuses on identity-based risks, safe disclosure environments, and inclusive, affirming practice.
outcomes: Understand DFV dynamics specific to LGBTQIA+ communities
Create safe and inclusive environments for disclosure
Apply affirming, respectful, and identity-safe practice

title: Working with Older People
description: This module supports practitioners to recognise and respond to DFV affecting older people, including elder abuse, dependency dynamics, and age-related vulnerabilities. It focuses on safe engagement and tailored support.
outcomes: Recognise DFV and elder abuse affecting older people
Understand age-related risks and dependency dynamics
Provide safe, respectful, and tailored support

title: Working with People Using Violence from Diverse Backgrounds
description: This module supports practitioners to work safely and effectively with people using violence from diverse cultural, social, and identity backgrounds. It focuses on accountability, cultural context, and safe behaviour change engagement.
outcomes: Understand how cultural and identity factors shape the use of violence
Engage safely with people using violence from diverse backgrounds
Promote accountability and behaviour change in culturally informed ways

title: Working with People with Disability
description: This module supports practitioners to work safely and respectfully with people with disability experiencing DFV. It focuses on disability-specific risks, communication needs, and accessible, rights-based practice.
outcomes: Recognise disability-specific DFV risks and barriers
Apply accessible and rights-based approaches
Support safe communication and autonomy

title: Working With Perpetrators
description: This module equips specialist DFV practitioners with the skills required to safely and ethically engage with people who use violence. It focuses on accountability frameworks, behaviour change principles, and risk‑aware engagement strategies that prioritise victim‑survivor safety.
outcomes: Engage safely and ethically with people who use violence
Apply accountability‑focused approaches that prioritise survivor safety
Understand behaviour change principles and their limitations in DFV contexts

title: Working with Police and Justice Agencies
description: This module supports practitioners to collaborate effectively with police, courts, and justice agencies. It focuses on reporting pathways, evidence, risk assessment, and coordinated justice responses.
outcomes: Understand police roles and responsibilities in DFV matters
Collaborate effectively with justice agencies
Support clients through reporting, evidence, and risk processes

title: Workplace and Community Organisation Responses
description: This module equips workplaces, clubs, and community organisations to recognise DFV, support affected members, and create safe organisational cultures. It focuses on policies, safe responses, and building supportive environments.
outcomes: Recognise DFV indicators within workplaces and community organisations
Respond safely and appropriately to disclosures or concerns
Develop policies and practices that promote safety and support

title: Youth Leadership and DFV Prevention
description: This module empowers young people to take active roles in preventing domestic and family violence within their communities. It focuses on youth leadership, respectful relationships, and building peer-led initiatives that promote safety and equality.
outcomes: Understand the role of young people in DFV prevention
Promote respectful relationships and challenge harmful norms
Lead or participate in youth-driven DFV prevention initiatives

title: DFV Parent Support Stream
description: A structured support pathway for parents experiencing domestic and family violence. This stream strengthens safety, parenting capacity, emotional stability, and child wellbeing through practical, trauma‑informed modules.
outcomes: Increase parental safety and stability
Strengthen parent–child connection
Support children’s emotional recovery
Build long‑term family resilience

title: DFV Peer Mentor Stream
description: Training for lived‑experience peer mentors supporting survivors of domestic and family violence. This stream builds safe peer‑support skills, boundaries, emotional safety, and trauma‑informed communication.
outcomes: Understand the peer mentor role and its limitations
Use lived experience safely and ethically
Maintain strong boundaries and personal wellbeing
Support survivors through safe, strengths‑based peer practice

title: DFV Practitioner Stream
description: A comprehensive training pathway for frontline domestic and family violence practitioners. This stream builds foundational DFV knowledge, assessment skills, trauma‑informed engagement, case management capability, and multi‑agency collaboration skills.
outcomes: Develop strong foundational DFV knowledge
Conduct safe and effective DFV assessments
Engage clients using trauma‑informed practice
Collaborate effectively across services
Manage complex DFV cases with confidence

title: DFV Behaviour‑Change Stream (People Who Use Violence)
description: A structured behaviour‑change pathway designed for people who use violence. This stream focuses on accountability, insight development, emotional regulation, respectful relationship skills, and sustainable behaviour change.
outcomes: Increase accountability for harmful behaviour
Develop emotional regulation and self‑management skills
Build respectful relationship practices
Support long‑term behaviour change and relapse prevention

title: DFV Specialist Intervention Stream
description: An advanced training pathway for specialist DFV practitioners working with high‑risk, complex, and multi‑layered domestic and family violence cases. This stream focuses on lethality assessment, multi‑agency risk panels, advanced trauma practice, and system navigation for clients facing intersecting barriers.
outcomes: Conduct advanced lethality and dynamic risk assessments
Manage complex DFV cases involving multiple risk factors
Work effectively within multi‑agency risk panels
Support clients navigating intersecting systemic barriers
Apply advanced trauma‑informed specialist interventions

description: This course supports fathers who are currently incarcerated to maintain safe, child-centred connection with their children. It focuses on emotional presence, respectful communication, and understanding the child’s experience during parental imprisonment.
learningOutcomes: Understand how imprisonment affects children emotionally and developmentally.
Learn safe ways to maintain connection through letters, calls, or supervised visits.
Recognise behaviours that support or harm a child’s sense of safety.
Develop skills for emotional presence and respectful communication.

modules.title: Understanding the Child’s Experience
modules.content: Explores how children process parental imprisonment and what they need to feel safe.

modules.title: Maintaining Safe Connection
modules.content: Covers letters, calls, supervised visits, and child-centred communication.

modules.title: Preparing for Reconnection
modules.content: Provides guidance on emotional readiness, accountability, and safe expectations.

title: Fathers Returning From Prison
description: This course supports fathers transitioning back into family and community life after incarceration. It focuses on rebuilding trust, understanding children’s needs, managing expectations, and creating safe, stable routines that support long-term change.
learningOutcomes: Understand the emotional and practical challenges of returning from prison.
Recognise the impact of incarceration on children and family relationships.
Learn strategies for rebuilding trust and stability.
Develop safe routines and behaviour patterns that support long-term change.

modules.title: The Transition Home
modules.content: Explores emotional, social, and practical challenges fathers face after release.

modules.title: Reconnecting With Children
modules.content: Focuses on child safety, emotional needs, and rebuilding trust slowly and respectfully.

modules.title: Building Safe Routines
modules.content: Provides tools for structure, accountability, and long-term behaviour change.

title: Fathers Navigating Supervised Contact
description: This course supports fathers to understand the purpose of supervised contact, how to engage safely, and how to use supervised time to rebuild trust with children. It focuses on emotional regulation, child‑centred behaviour, and working respectfully with supervisors.
learningOutcomes: Understand the purpose and safety role of supervised contact.
Learn how to engage in supervised visits in a child‑centred and respectful way.
Recognise behaviours that build or damage trust during supervised time.
Develop emotional regulation strategies to stay calm and present.

modules.title: Why Supervised Contact Happens
modules.content: Explains safety concerns, court decisions, and the role of supervision in protecting children.

modules.title: Making the Most of Supervised Time
modules.content: Focuses on child‑centred behaviour, emotional presence, and building trust.

modules.title: Working With Supervisors
modules.content: Provides guidance on respectful communication, following instructions, and demonstrating accountability.

sections.content: This lesson introduces respectful communication in a warm, supportive way. Many parents struggle with this area, and it is completely normal. You will learn why this topic matters, how it affects your child's development, and what you can expect to gain from the lesson.
sections.title: Welcome and Orientation

sections.content: This section explains the core ideas behind respectful communication in simple, parent-friendly language. You will learn what the concept means, why it matters, how it affects your child's brain and behavior, and how stress or trauma can influence this area.

sections.content: This final section helps you integrate respectful communication into everyday life. You will reflect on what you learned, choose one small action to try this week, and consider how the skill can support your family's wellbeing.

sections.content: This lesson introduces managing challenging behaviour in a warm, supportive way. Many parents struggle with this area, and it is completely normal. You will learn why this topic matters, how it affects your child's development, and what you can expect to gain from the lesson.
sections.title: Welcome and Orientation

sections.content: This section explains the core ideas behind managing challenging behaviour in simple, parent-friendly language. You will learn what the concept means, why it matters, how it affects your child's brain and behavior, and how stress or trauma can influence this area.
sections.title: Core Concepts

sections.content: Here you will find practical, step-by-step strategies for applying managing challenging behaviour in real life. These skills are designed to be clear, doable, and supportive. You will get examples, scripts you can use with your child, and guidance for staying calm and consistent.
sections.title: Practical Skills and Strategies

sections.content: This activity helps you and your child practice managing challenging behaviour together. It is simple, achievable, and designed to build connection. You will receive a guided exercise and a reflection prompt to help you notice what worked well.
sections.title: Parent Child Practice Activity

sections.content: This final section helps you integrate managing challenging behaviour into everyday life. You will reflect on what you learned, choose one small action to try this week, and consider how the skill can support your family's wellbeing.
sections.title: Reflection and Integration

It supports safer, more consistent caregiving by improving understanding, strengthening emotional connection, and reducing stress in daily routines. This topic is suitable for parents who need guidance in applying positive parenting strategies and may benefit families working toward stability, reunification, or improved home safety.

sections.content: This lesson introduces working with families in a warm, supportive way. Many parents struggle with this area, and it is completely normal. You will learn why this topic matters, how it affects your child's development, and what you can expect to gain from the lesson.
sections.title: Welcome and Orientation

sections.content: This section explains the core ideas behind working with families in simple, parent-friendly language. You will learn what the concept means, why it matters, how it affects your child's brain and behavior, and how stress or trauma can influence this area.
sections.title: Core Concepts

sections.content: Here you will find practical, step-by-step strategies for applying working with families in real life. These skills are designed to be clear, doable, and supportive. You will get examples, scripts you can use with your child, and guidance for staying calm and consistent.
sections.title: Practical Skills and Strategies

sections.content: This activity helps you and your child practice working with families together. It is simple, achievable, and designed to build connection. You will receive a guided exercise and a reflection prompt to help you notice what worked well.
sections.title: Parent Child Practice Activity

sections.content: This final section helps you integrate working with families into everyday life. You will reflect on what you learned, choose one small action to try this week, and consider how the skill can support your family's wellbeing.
sections.title: Reflection and Integration

title: Alcohol and Other Drugs (AOD) and DFV
description: Explores how substance use and DFV interact, including risk, safety, and support options.
learningOutcomes: Understand the relationship between AOD and DFV.
Recognise increased risks for parents and children.
Identify support options for safety and recovery.
caseworkerSummary: Helps parents understand how AOD and DFV interact and how to seek support.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.content: AOD and DFV often overlap, increasing risk for families.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content: Substance use does not cause DFV, but it can escalate harm and reduce safety.

sections.title: Practical Skills
sections.content: Parents learn how to access AOD support and plan for safety.

sections.title: Activity
sections.content: Reflect on how AOD has affected safety in your family.

sections.title: Reflection
sections.content: Understanding the connection helps parents make informed choices.

title: Child Protection Basics
description: Explains how child protection systems work, why they become involved, and what parents can expect.
learningOutcomes: Understand the role of child protection.
Recognise why DFV triggers involvement.
Identify ways to work constructively with services.
caseworkerSummary: Helps parents understand child protection processes and expectations.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.content: Child protection involvement can feel frightening. This lesson explains why it happens.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content: DFV is a major risk factor because it affects childrenâ€™s safety and wellbeing.

sections.title: Practical Skills
sections.content: Parents learn how to communicate with workers and demonstrate protective actions.

sections.title: Activity
sections.content: Reflect on what you want child protection to understand about your situation.

sections.title: Reflection
sections.content: Understanding the system helps reduce fear and build collaboration.

title: Child Safety Planning
description: Provides practical strategies for creating safety plans with and for children during DFV situations.
learningOutcomes: Understand what child safety planning involves.
Identify ageâ€‘appropriate strategies.
Create a personalised safety plan.
caseworkerSummary: Supports parents to create practical, ageâ€‘appropriate safety plans for children.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.content: Safety planning helps children know what to do during unsafe moments.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content: Plans must be simple, ageâ€‘appropriate, and focused on getting to safetyâ€”not intervening.

sections.title: Practical Skills
sections.content: Parents learn how to create safe rooms, exit routes, and code words.

sections.title: Activity
sections.content: Draft a simple safety plan for your child based on their age.

sections.title: Reflection
sections.content: Safety planning empowers children without placing responsibility on them.

title: Understanding Coercive Control
description: A deep look at coercive controlâ€”how it works, why itâ€™s dangerous, and how it affects parents and children.
learningOutcomes: Define coercive control and its key components.
Recognise non-physical forms of abuse.
Understand how coercive control impacts childrenâ€™s safety and wellbeing.
caseworkerSummary: Explains coercive control and helps parents identify subtle but harmful patterns of domination.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.content: Coercive control is one of the most harmful forms of DFV. It often happens without physical violence.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content: Coercive control includes monitoring, isolation, threats, manipulation, and restricting freedom or choices.

sections.title: Practical Skills
sections.content: Parents learn to map controlling behaviours and understand how they create fear and dependency.

sections.title: Activity
sections.content: Identify behaviours that made you feel small, scared, or controlled. These may be signs of coercive control.

sections.title: Reflection
sections.content: Recognising coercive control helps parents understand their experiences and seek appropriate support.

title: Family Law Basics
description: Provides an overview of family law processes, parenting arrangements, and how DFV is considered in legal decisions.
learningOutcomes: Understand key family law concepts.
Recognise how DFV affects legal decisions.
Identify ways to prepare for legal processes.
caseworkerSummary: Gives parents a basic understanding of family law and how DFV is considered.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.content: Family law can feel overwhelming. This lesson explains the basics.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content: Topics include parenting orders, mediation, and how DFV influences decisions.

sections.title: Practical Skills
sections.content: Parents learn how to prepare documents, timelines, and evidence.

sections.title: Activity
sections.content: List any legal questions or concerns you have.

sections.title: Reflection
sections.content: Understanding the system helps reduce fear and confusion.

title: Financial Abuse
description: Explains how financial control, restriction, and exploitation are used as forms of domestic and family violence.
learningOutcomes: Recognise forms of financial abuse.
Understand how financial control limits safety.
Identify strategies to increase financial independence.
caseworkerSummary: Helps parents identify financial abuse and begin planning for financial safety.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.content: Financial abuse is one of the most common and powerful forms of DFV.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content: It includes restricting access to money, monitoring spending, debt manipulation, and sabotaging employment.

sections.title: Practical Skills
sections.content: Parents learn steps like securing documents, opening safe accounts, and tracking income.

sections.title: Activity
sections.content: Identify any financial behaviours that made you feel controlled or restricted.

sections.title: Reflection
sections.content: Financial safety is a key part of longâ€‘term independence.

title: Healthy Future Relationships
description: Explores what healthy relationships look like and how parents can build safe, respectful connections in the future.
learningOutcomes: Recognise the qualities of healthy relationships.
Identify red flags and green flags.
Build confidence in future relationship choices.
caseworkerSummary: Helps parents understand healthy relationships and rebuild trust in future connections.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.content: After DFV, it can be hard to trust again. This lesson explores what healthy relationships look like.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content: Healthy relationships include respect, communication, boundaries, and equality.

sections.title: Practical Skills
sections.content: Parents learn to identify red flags and green flags in future relationships.

sections.title: Activity
sections.content: List qualities you want in future relationships.

sections.title: Reflection
sections.content: You deserve relationships that are safe, respectful, and supportive.

title: Impact of DFV on Children
description: Helps parents understand how domestic and family violence affects children emotionally, physically, and developmentally.
learningOutcomes: Recognise how DFV affects children.
Understand behavioural and emotional responses.
Identify ways to support childrenâ€™s healing.
caseworkerSummary: Supports parents to understand the effects of DFV on children and how to respond supportively.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.content: Children are deeply affected by DFV, even when they do not see the violence directly.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content: Children may show fear, anxiety, aggression, withdrawal, or developmental delays.

sections.title: Practical Skills
sections.content: Parents learn how to respond with safety, predictability, and emotional support.

sections.title: Activity
sections.content: Think about how your child reacts during stress. What might they be communicating?

sections.title: Reflection
sections.content: Understanding childrenâ€™s responses helps parents support healing.

title: Infant Trauma and DFV
description: Explores how domestic and family violence affects babies, including attachment, development, and stress responses.
learningOutcomes: Understand how infants experience trauma.
Recognise signs of stress in babies.
Identify ways to support infant safety and bonding.
caseworkerSummary: Helps parents understand how DFV affects babies and how to support early recovery.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.content: Babies are deeply affected by DFV, even though they cannot speak or understand events.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content: Infants absorb stress through disrupted routines, loud noises, fear, and caregiver distress.

sections.title: Practical Skills
sections.content: Parents learn to rebuild safety through calm routines, closeness, and predictable care.

sections.title: Activity
sections.content: Reflect on your babyâ€™s cuesâ€”crying, clinginess, sleep changes.

sections.title: Reflection
sections.content: Infants heal through safe, consistent, loving care.

title: Myths and Misconceptions About DFV
description: Challenges common myths about domestic and family violence to help parents understand the truth behind harmful stereotypes.
learningOutcomes: Identify common myths about DFV.
Understand how myths harm survivors.
Recognise the realities of DFV dynamics.
caseworkerSummary: Helps parents challenge internalised myths that may prevent helpâ€‘seeking or selfâ€‘recognition.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.content: Many parents carry myths about DFV that make it harder to recognise abuse or seek help.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content: Myths include 'DFV is caused by anger' or 'If it was really bad, they would leave'. These are false and harmful.

sections.title: Practical Skills
sections.content: Parents learn to replace myths with accurate, evidenceâ€‘based understanding.

sections.title: Activity
sections.content: Identify a myth you once believed. What changed your understanding?

sections.title: Reflection
sections.content: Letting go of myths helps parents see their situation clearly and make informed decisions.

title: Postâ€‘Separation Abuse
description: Explores how abuse can continue or escalate after separation, including legal, financial, and emotional tactics.
learningOutcomes: Recognise forms of postâ€‘separation abuse.
Understand how systems can be used to continue control.
Identify strategies for safety and documentation.
caseworkerSummary: Helps parents understand ongoing risks after separation and how to plan for safety.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.content: Abuse often continues after separation through new tactics.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content: Common tactics include harassment, stalking, legal abuse, and using children as tools of control.

sections.title: Practical Skills
sections.content: Parents learn documentation, boundaries, and safe communication strategies.

sections.title: Activity
sections.content: Reflect on any behaviours that continued or escalated after separation.

sections.title: Reflection
sections.content: Awareness helps parents protect themselves and their children.

title: Protective Parenting
description: Explains how parents can take protective actions to support childrenâ€™s safety, stability, and emotional wellbeing after DFV.
learningOutcomes: Understand what protective parenting means.
Recognise protective behaviours.
Apply strategies to support childrenâ€™s safety.
caseworkerSummary: Supports parents to understand and demonstrate protective behaviours.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.content: Protective parenting helps children feel safe, supported, and understood.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content: Protective actions include emotional availability, predictable routines, and safe boundaries.

sections.title: Practical Skills
sections.content: Parents learn how to respond calmly, validate feelings, and create safe environments.

sections.title: Activity
sections.content: Identify one protective action you already use with your child.

sections.title: Reflection
sections.content: Protective parenting strengthens healing and resilience.

title: Rebuilding Confidence
description: Supports parents to rebuild selfâ€‘worth, identity, and confidence after experiencing DFV.
learningOutcomes: Recognise how DFV impacts confidence.
Identify strengths and personal values.
Apply strategies to rebuild selfâ€‘belief.
caseworkerSummary: Helps parents rebuild confidence and identity after DFV.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.content: DFV often damages confidence and selfâ€‘belief. Healing includes rebuilding your sense of self.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content: Abusive behaviour can erode identity through criticism, control, and isolation.

sections.title: Practical Skills
sections.content: Parents learn strengthsâ€‘based reflection and small steps toward selfâ€‘trust.

sections.title: Activity
sections.content: List three strengths you have shown during difficult times.

sections.title: Reflection
sections.content: Confidence grows through small, consistent acts of selfâ€‘respect.

title: Recognising Abuse
description: Helps parents identify the full spectrum of abusive behaviours, including those that are subtle, hidden, or normalised.
learningOutcomes: Identify different types of abuse.
Recognise early warning signs.
Understand how abuse escalates over time.
caseworkerSummary: Supports parents to recognise abusive behaviours that may have been minimised or normalised.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.content: Abuse is not always obvious. Many parents only recognise it after learning the signs.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content: Abuse can be emotional, financial, sexual, physical, or digital. It often escalates gradually.

sections.title: Practical Skills
sections.content: Parents learn to identify patterns such as gaslighting, intimidation, and financial restriction.

sections.title: Activity
sections.content: List behaviours that made you feel unsafe or controlled. Compare them to the categories of abuse.

sections.title: Reflection
sections.content: Recognising abuse is a powerful step toward safety and healing.

title: Recovery and Healing
description: Helps parents understand the healing process after DFV and how to support themselves and their children.
learningOutcomes: Understand the stages of healing.
Recognise emotional and physical recovery needs.
Apply strategies for longâ€‘term wellbeing.
caseworkerSummary: Supports parents to understand healing and build longâ€‘term wellbeing.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.content: Healing from DFV takes time, support, and compassion.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content: Healing is not linear. It includes emotional, physical, and relational recovery.

sections.title: Practical Skills
sections.content: Parents learn grounding, selfâ€‘care, and supportâ€‘seeking strategies.

sections.title: Activity
sections.content: Identify one healing activity that helps you feel calmer or stronger.

sections.title: Reflection
sections.content: Recovery is a journey, not a destination.

title: Technologyâ€‘Facilitated Abuse
description: Explains how technology can be used to monitor, control, or harm parents and children, and how to increase digital safety.
learningOutcomes: Recognise forms of techâ€‘based abuse.
Identify risks in devices and accounts.
Apply practical digital safety strategies.
caseworkerSummary: Helps parents understand techâ€‘based abuse and improve digital safety.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.content: Technology can be used to support safetyâ€”or to cause harm.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content: Tech abuse includes tracking, monitoring, hacking, impersonation, and harassment.

sections.title: Practical Skills
sections.content: Parents learn to secure accounts, update passwords, and check devices for risks.

sections.title: Activity
sections.content: Review your devices and accounts. Identify any that may need securing.

sections.title: Reflection
sections.content: Digital safety is an important part of overall safety planning.

title: Traumaâ€‘Informed Parenting
description: Helps parents understand trauma responses in themselves and their children, and how to create safety, connection, and predictability.
learningOutcomes: Understand trauma responses in adults and children.
Recognise triggers and stress reactions.
Apply traumaâ€‘informed strategies at home.
caseworkerSummary: Supports parents to understand trauma and apply traumaâ€‘informed strategies at home.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.content: Trauma affects how parents and children think, feel, and behave. This lesson builds understanding and compassion.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content: Trauma responses include fight, flight, freeze, and fawn. These are survival instincts, not choices.

sections.title: Practical Skills
sections.content: Parents learn grounding, predictable routines, and coâ€‘regulation strategies.

sections.title: Activity
sections.content: Identify a moment when you or your child felt overwhelmed. What helped?

sections.title: Reflection
sections.content: Traumaâ€‘informed parenting strengthens safety and connection.

title: What Is Domestic and Family Violence?
description: An introduction to domestic and family violence, explaining the different forms it can take and how it affects parents, children, and families.
learningOutcomes: Understand the definition and forms of domestic and family violence.
Recognise the difference between conflict and abuse.
Identify early warning signs of controlling or harmful behaviour.
caseworkerSummary: Provides parents with a foundational understanding of DFV, including types of abuse and early indicators of risk.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.content: Domestic and family violence can be confusing and overwhelming. This lesson helps parents understand what DFV actually is and why recognising it matters.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content: DFV includes emotional, physical, financial, sexual, and psychological abuse. It is about power and control, not anger or conflict.

sections.title: Practical Skills
sections.content: Parents learn how to identify patterns of behaviour that signal risk, including isolation, intimidation, and monitoring.

sections.title: Activity
sections.content: Reflect on behaviours youâ€™ve seen or experienced. Which ones align with DFV patterns?

sections.title: Reflection
sections.content: Understanding DFV is the first step toward safety, healing, and informed decisionâ€‘making.

title: Why Leaving Can Be Dangerous
description: Explains why the period around separation is often the most dangerous time for victim-survivors and how to plan for safety.
learningOutcomes: Understand why risk increases during separation.
Recognise common escalation patterns.
Identify strategies for safer planning.
caseworkerSummary: Helps parents understand why separation increases risk and how to plan for safety.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.content: Leaving an abusive relationship is often the most dangerous time. This lesson explains why risk increases.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content: Abusive partners may escalate threats, stalking, or violence when they feel they are losing control.

sections.title: Practical Skills
sections.content: Parents learn strategies for safer planning, including timing, support networks, and documentation.

sections.title: Activity
sections.content: Reflect on any behaviours that escalated during past attempts to leave.

sections.title: Reflection
sections.content: Understanding risk helps parents make informed, safer decisions.

title: Why People Stay
description: Explores the complex reasons why people remain in abusive relationships, reducing shame and increasing understanding.
learningOutcomes: Understand the barriers to leaving abusive relationships.
Recognise the role of fear, coercion, and survival strategies.
Reduce selfâ€‘blame and shame.
caseworkerSummary: Supports parents to understand that staying is often a survival strategy, not a failure.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.content: Leaving an abusive relationship is complex. Many parents stay because it feels safer than leaving.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content: Barriers include fear, financial dependence, threats, manipulation, and concern for childrenâ€™s safety.

sections.title: Practical Skills
sections.content: Parents learn to identify survival strategies and understand their own choices with compassion.

sections.title: Activity
sections.content: Reflect on reasons that made leaving difficult. These are valid and understandable.

sections.title: Reflection
sections.content: Understanding why people stay reduces shame and opens the door to safer planning.

Behaviour Change
description: Explores how behaviour change works, what supports it, and how to build sustainable new habits.
learningOutcomes: Understand the stages of behaviour change.
Recognise barriers to change.
Apply strategies to build new habits.
caseworkerSummary: Supports participants to understand the process of change and build new, safer behaviours.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.content: Change is possible when you understand what drives your behaviour.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content: Behaviour change requires motivation, consistency, and accountability.

sections.title: Practical Skills
sections.content: Participants learn habitâ€‘building, goalâ€‘setting, and selfâ€‘monitoring techniques.

sections.title: Activity
sections.content: Identify one behaviour you want to change and why.

sections.title: Reflection
sections.content: Change is a process, not a single decision.

title: Conflict Resolution
description: Provides strategies for resolving conflict safely, respectfully, and without using power or control.
learningOutcomes: Recognise healthy and unhealthy conflict patterns.
Understand how conflict escalates.
Apply strategies for safe conflict resolution.
caseworkerSummary: Supports participants to resolve conflict without using violence or control.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.content: Conflict is normal, but how we handle it determines whether harm occurs.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content: Unresolved conflict can escalate into harmful behaviour.

sections.title: Practical Skills
sections.content: Participants learn negotiation, compromise, and deâ€‘escalation skills.

sections.title: Activity
sections.content: Identify a conflict pattern you want to change.

sections.title: Reflection
sections.content: Healthy conflict resolution strengthens relationships.

title: Emotional Regulation
description: Helps participants understand emotional triggers, responses, and strategies to regulate emotions safely.
learningOutcomes: Recognise emotional triggers and responses.

title: Small Changes, Big Impact
learningGoal: Learn how small behaviour changes can reduce harm and increase control.
microLesson: Change doesn’t have to be dramatic to be meaningful. Even small shifts—like delaying use, reducing quantity, or changing your environment—can create momentum. Today you’ll choose one small change to try.
activity: Write down one small change you can make this week to reduce harm or increase control.

title: Weekly Reflection & Next Steps
learningGoal: Consolidate learning from Week 1 and prepare for Week 2.
microLesson: You’ve spent the week building insight into your patterns, triggers, and safety strategies. Today is about pulling everything together and setting yourself up for next week’s focus on cravings and coping skills.
activity: Write one thing you learned this week and one goal you want to focus on next week.

title: Understanding Substance Use
learningGoal: Understand what substance use is and why patterns develop.
microLesson: Overview of substance use, reasons people use, and how habits form.
activity: Write down your personal goals for this AOD program.

title: Your Substance Use Patterns
learningGoal: Reflect on your personal patterns, habits, and the role substance use plays in your life.
microLesson: Everyone’s relationship with substances is different. Some use to cope with stress, others to numb emotions, and some out of routine. Today is about honestly exploring your own patterns without judgement.
activity: Describe when you most commonly use substances: time of day, emotional state, and who you’re usually with.

title: How Substance Use Affects Relationships
learningGoal: Explore how substance use impacts relationships, communication, and trust.
microLesson: Substance use can strain relationships, especially when communication breaks down or trust is damaged. Today is about recognising these impacts without blame, and identifying where repair may be needed.
activity: Write one relationship you want to improve and one step you could take to rebuild trust.

title: Staying Safe
learningGoal: Understand harm minimisation and create a basic personal safety plan.
microLesson: Harm minimisation is about staying as safe as possible, even if you’re not ready to stop using. This includes using less, using slower, avoiding mixing substances, and having support available.
activity: Write three harm‑minimisation strategies you can use immediately.

title: Understanding Triggers
learningGoal: Identify internal and external triggers that influence substance use.
microLesson: Triggers can be people, places, emotions, or situations that increase the urge to use. Learning to spot them early gives you more control. Today you’ll explore the triggers that show up most often in your life.
activity: List three internal triggers (thoughts or feelings) and three external triggers (people, places, or situations) that affect you.

title: What Are Cravings?
learningGoal: Understand what cravings are and why they happen.
microLesson: Cravings are intense urges that come from the brain seeking relief, comfort, or familiarity. They can feel physical, emotional, or both. Today is about understanding what cravings actually are so you can respond instead of react.
activity: Describe what cravings feel like for you: physical sensations, thoughts, and emotions.

title: What Is Substance Use?
